issues.legal_issue: A purported guardian who is not legally recognized as a guardian cannot validly alienate a minor’s separate property merely by managing the minor’s affairs.
material_facts: A minor inherited a share of property from her father, and the property was not joint family property.
The minor’s sister, who was not a guardian within the statutory definition, purported to act as the minor’s guardian and sold the minor’s share to a purchaser.
The purchaser took possession under the sale, and the minor’s later purchaser claimed the minor’s share under a subsequent sale deed.
issues.conclusion: The sister’s sale of the minor’s share was void, and the first purchaser acquired no interest in it. The sale was prohibited irrespective of whether it was for legal necessity; the ruling on joint-family property was unnecessary because the property was not joint family property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(b), 6 and 11 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, a sister who is not a legally recognized guardian cannot deal with a minor’s property merely as a de facto guardian or manager; Section 11 prohibits such a disposition, which is void ab initio. Section 8 provides for a natural guardian’s powers and for dispositions in contravention of its requirements to be voidable, but that regime does not validate a de facto manager’s disposition under Section 11. The Court relied on Kondamudi Sriramulu v. Myneni Pundarikakshayya, which described a de facto guardian as a de facto manager, and Ganayya v. Radhabai, which applied Section 11’s prohibition. It distinguished Sri Narayan Bal v. Sridhar Sutar because that case concerned an undivided interest in joint family property, and noted that the pre-Act rule in Hunooman Persaud Pandey’s case did not survive the statutory prohibition.

rule.if: property_title_proceeding and minor_owned_separate_property and transferor_was_not_legal_guardian and transferor_managed_minor_estate

predicates.property_title_proceeding: The case is a proceeding concerning title to property transferred on behalf of a minor.
predicates.minor_owned_separate_property: The minor owned property that was not an undivided interest in joint family property.
predicates.transferor_was_not_legal_guardian: The person who made the transfer was not legally recognized as the minor’s guardian.
predicates.transferor_managed_minor_estate: The transferor had taken on the management of the minor’s estate and purported to transfer the minor’s property.

issues.definition: When a property-title proceeding concerns a minor’s separate property transferred by someone who was not a legal guardian but managed the minor’s estate, the transfer is void.

issues.legal_issue: A minor need not bring a suit to set aside a void transfer made by a de facto manager, and a lawful disposition after attaining majority may demonstrate repudiation of that transfer.
material_facts: The minor attained majority after her sister had purported to sell her share.
After attaining majority, she sold her share to another purchaser by a registered deed.
The lower courts treated the earlier sale as voidable and concluded that it had become confirmed because she had not challenged it within three years of attaining majority.
There was no finding that she had ratified the earlier transfer.
issues.conclusion: The invalid transfer did not have to be set aside by a suit or other judicial proceeding. The former minor’s later lawful sale asserting her title was sufficient to show repudiation, and the High Court was justified in granting partition and separate possession to the later purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: A transfer prohibited by Section 11 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, is void and does not require a suit or judicial proceeding to set it aside. On attaining majority, the former minor may repudiate it in any manner when occasion arises; a lawful transfer of the property asserting the former minor’s title is sufficient. The Court also observed that there was no finding of ratification, even assuming ratification could cure the defect.

rule.if: property_title_proceeding and prior_transfer_by_de_facto_manager and former_minor_attained_majority and former_minor_lawfully_transferred_property_asserting_title

predicates.property_title_proceeding: The case is a proceeding concerning title to property previously transferred on behalf of a minor.
predicates.prior_transfer_by_de_facto_manager: A person who was not a legal guardian but managed the minor’s estate had previously transferred the minor’s property.
predicates.former_minor_attained_majority: The minor whose property was transferred later attained majority.
predicates.former_minor_lawfully_transferred_proper: After attaining majority, the former minor lawfully transferred the property while asserting ownership of it.

issues.definition: When a former minor lawfully transfers property while asserting title after attaining majority, the earlier transfer by a de facto manager need not be set aside and is repudiated.
